biomarkers.name: Ki-67
biomarkers.prevalence: Usually low, often <5% in typical carcinoid; not a formal WHO definitional criterion in lung carcinoids
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports distinction from higher-grade neuroendocrine neoplasms; typical vs atypical carcinoid are defined primarily by mitotic count and necrosis rather than Ki-67 alone

biomarkers.name: SSTR2 expression
biomarkers.clinical_use: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET for staging; PRRT (177Lu-DOTATATE) in advanced somatostatin-receptor-positive disease; long-acting somatostatin analogues for symptom control and sometimes tumor control

biomarkers.name: Chromogranin A
biomarkers.clinical_use: Monitoring in selected patients; affected by PPI use and renal function

biomarkers.name: 5-HIAA (24h urine)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnosis and monitoring of carcinoid syndrome

biomarkers.name: MEN1, ARID1A, EIF1AX
biomarkers.prevalence: Recurrent alterations reported; no single pathognomonic driver and no established targetable fusion hallmark
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports known pulmonary carcinoid molecular profile; distinguishes from SCLC/LCNEC biology

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Organoid, trabecular, or nested growth of uniform round cells with 'salt and pepper' chromatin
variants: typical carcinoid (mitoses <2/2 mm² and no necrosis)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Low-grade (WHO); Ki-67 usually low but not required for WHO grading/typing

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Pulmonary neuroendocrine cells (PNEC) — same broad lineage as other pulmonary neuroendocrine neoplasms but biologically distinct from SCLC/LCNEC
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Endoderm — foregut derivative with neuroendocrine differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine — synaptophysin+, chromogranin+, often SSTR2-positive; low proliferative activity
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Position on well-differentiated end of pulmonary NET spectrum; DIPNECH (diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia) is a recognized precursor lesion in some cases
